request.message: I have recycled polypropylene packaging flakes. Each delivery has a different mix and sometimes paper label scraps in unknown amounts. I want to make a low-cost indoor entrance mat with good grip. I only have hand tools at home, no lab or heated press. What can I do when the input changes?

response.reply: You want a low-cost indoor entrance mat with good grip from variable flakes, using only hand tools. I drafted only what you stated - please review it before use. Since the mix changes, the useful next move is a small observation and paper comparison of no-heat ways to contain the flakes. See questions and first step.

questions: When you say good grip, is the priority shoes gripping the top, the mat staying still on the floor, or both - and what is your entrance floor made of?
With only hand tools and no heat, how were you thinking to hold loose flakes together - for example in a sewn pocket, glued to a backing, or another way?
For your current delivery, what does the mix look like and do you want to remove paper label scraps or use the flakes as-is?
response.first_step: From your current delivery, hand-sort one small bowl to note flake size/shape and paper share, and sketch your indoor entrance with mat size and floor type. Use that to compare no-heat containment ideas on paper for grip and cleaning, and line up a bench tilt comparison of tiny contained samples against a shoe sole - do not step on loose flakes or an untested mat to test it.
